reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure, let iota be any finite type, let nu be any probability measure on E × E, let xstar belong to E, and let h and M be nonnegative real numbers. Assume that (x,p) ↦ ‖x-xstar‖²+‖p‖² is nu-integrable with integral at most M. Set a = exp(-h/2), sigma = sqrt(1-exp(-h)), and mu = (nu.prod(stdGaussian E)).prod(Measure.pi(fun _ : iota => stdGaussian E)). For w = (((x,p),z),g), define X(w)=x, P0(w)=a p+sigma z, and G_j(w)=g(j), where multiplication of a vector by a real number means scalar multiplication. Set B=M+(1-exp(-h)) dim_R(E). Then B is nonnegative, X and P0 are measurable, and w ↦ ‖X(w)-xstar‖²+‖P0(w)‖² is mu-integrable with integral at most B. Moreover, for every j in iota, G_j is measurable and w ↦ ‖G_j(w)‖² is mu-integrable with integral equal to dim_R(E).
objects: The incoming joint probability law nu; reference point xstar; refresh parameters a and sigma; product probability measure mu; coordinate maps X and G_j; refreshed momentum map P0; and scalar bound B. Incoming energy is ‖x-xstar‖²+‖p‖², and refreshed energy is ‖X-xstar‖²+‖P0‖².
domains: E is a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space. iota is a finite type. nu is a probability measure on E × E. xstar belongs to E, and h,M are nonnegative real numbers. mu is a measure on ((E × E) × E) × (iota → E). X,P0,G_j take values in E; both energy functions and B are real-valued.
quantifiers: Universally quantify E with the stated structures, finite iota, incoming probability law nu, xstar in E, and nonnegative h,M. Assuming the incoming energy is integrable with integral at most M, all conclusions hold for the displayed definitions. The measurability and squared-norm integral conclusions for G_j hold for every j in iota.
assumptions: Completeness, finite real dimension, real inner-product structure, and Borel measurable structure for E; finiteness of iota; nu being a probability measure; h≥0 and M≥0; nu-integrability of (x,p) ↦ ‖x-xstar‖²+‖p‖²; and its nu-integral being at most M. The incoming position and momentum need not be independent. Independence of the Gaussian factors from the incoming pair and from one another comes from the product measure construction.
conclusion: B≥0. X and P0 are measurable. Refreshed energy is mu-integrable and its mu-integral is at most B. For every j, G_j is measurable and ‖G_j‖² is mu-integrable with mu-integral exactly dim_R(E).
scopes: These are ordinary explicitly defined coordinate functions, not quotient classes or selected representatives. Integrability is global under the indicated measures. The energy bound is an integral bound, not a pointwise upper bound. The Gaussian moment equality applies to each individual index, not to a sum over indices. The statement covers empty iota, when its indexed conclusions are vacuous. No iterative algorithm, convergence claim, or multi-step bound is asserted.
constant_dependencies: a and sigma depend only on h. B depends only on M,h, and dim_R(E), with no explicit dependence on nu,xstar, or the cardinality of iota. Each Gaussian squared-norm integral equals dim_R(E). The incoming energy assumption depends on nu and xstar, while the refreshed energy also depends on h through P0.
